definition: A practice of pausing for several seconds before answering another person's request.
The habit of writing a private summary after taking part in a group discussion.
A rule that changes which group member speaks first at each meeting.
A practice of requesting another explanation before accepting a proposal.
A routine in which a group spends the first ten minutes of a meeting in silence.
The practice of looking over a completed task again on the following day.
The custom of leaving a short note rather than speaking when entering a shared room.
The act of silently rehearsing an answer before saying it aloud.
The practice of recording each change made during a shared task.
A routine in which group members contribute to a discussion in a fixed order.
The habit of replying to a social invitation after checking other plans first.
The habit of asking for an additional opinion after a decision has been made.
The custom of leaving one seat unoccupied during a group gathering.
The practice of making an individual draft before beginning a shared task.
The act of repeating another person's instructions in different words before carrying them out.
The practice of giving a planned comment after a group discussion has finished rather than during it.
A custom in which the person choosing a group's meeting place rotates each time.
